title: The Song of Solomon Timeline
sub: Love Is as Strong as Death · I Am My Beloved's, and He Is Mine
desc: An extended poetic dialogue between two lovers celebrates romantic and physical intimacy without an ounce of allegorical hedging, closing in one of Scripture's most quoted statements on love's unquenchable power.

eras.label: Era One · Song of Solomon 1
eras.name: Let Him Kiss Me — Dark but Lovely
eras.dates: An extended dialogue between two lovers opens the Bible's only book devoted entirely to romantic and physical love, with almost no narrative frame at all

events.title: Let Him Kiss Me With the Kisses of His Mouth
events.detail: The Beloved opens with an unguarded desire for her lover's kisses, describes herself as sun-darkened from vineyard work, and the two exchange increasingly intimate praise for one another in a poem with almost no narrative framework at all — just voices in dialogue.

verses.text: “Oh, how I wish you would kiss me passionately! For your lovemaking is more delightful than wine.”

eras.label: Era Two · Song of Solomon 2
eras.name: I Am My Lover's, and He Is Mine
eras.dates: Nature imagery of spring's arrival frames a growing intimacy, closing with a formula of mutual belonging that recurs throughout the book

events.title: The Winter Has Passed — My Lover Is Mine and I Am His
events.detail: The lover arrives like a gazelle bounding over mountains, calling his beloved to come away now that winter has passed and spring has arrived, and the chapter closes with the book's first statement of the mutual belonging that will recur as a refrain.

verses.text: “My lover is mine and I am his; he grazes among the lilies.”

eras.label: Era Three · Song of Solomon 3
eras.name: A Night Search — Solomon's Wedding Procession
eras.dates: A dream or memory of a nighttime search for a missing lover gives way to a lavish description of a royal wedding procession

events.title: I Searched for Him, but I Did Not Find Him
events.detail: The Beloved searches the nighttime city streets for her missing lover, finally finding him and refusing to let go, in an anxious dream-or-memory sequence.

verses.text: “Scarcely had I passed them by when I found my beloved! I held onto him tightly and would not let him go.”

events.title: Solomon's Portable Couch — a Royal Wedding Procession
events.detail: A lavish royal wedding procession arrives, Solomon's ornate sedan chair guarded by sixty warriors, and the maidens of Zion are called out to gaze on the king crowned on the most joyous day of his life.

verses.text: “Come out, O maidens of Zion, and gaze upon King Solomon! He is wearing the crown… on the most joyous day of his life!”

eras.label: Era Four · Song of Solomon 4
eras.name: You Are Altogether Beautiful — a Locked Garden
eras.dates: An extended head-to-toe description of the beloved's body builds toward a garden metaphor for physical intimacy

events.title: You Are a Locked Garden, My Sister, My Bride
events.detail: The lover praises his beloved's body from head to toe in extended poetic imagery, declaring her altogether beautiful and without blemish, before comparing her to a locked garden and sealed spring — an image of intimacy reserved and then invited.

verses.text: “You are altogether beautiful, my darling! There is no blemish in you!”

eras.label: Era Five · Song of Solomon 5
eras.name: I Have Entered My Garden — a Missed Encounter and a Second Search
eras.dates: Consummated intimacy is followed by a painful scene of miscommunication, longing, and mistreatment by the city watchmen

events.title: I Have Entered My Garden — Eat, Friends, and Drink Freely
events.detail: The garden imagery of the previous chapter resolves into consummated intimacy, celebrated with an invitation for the couple's friends to eat and drink freely alongside them.

verses.text: “I have entered my garden, O my sister, my bride… Eat, friends, and drink! Drink freely, O lovers!”

events.title: I Looked for Him but Did Not Find Him — the Watchmen's Cruelty
events.detail: A moment's hesitation costs the Beloved her lover's presence at the door, and her search for him through the city ends painfully when the watchmen beat and mistreat her, followed by an extended catalog of the lover's beauty to the maidens of Jerusalem.

verses.text: “The watchmen found me as they made their rounds in the city. They beat me; they bruised me; they took away my cloak.”

eras.label: Era Six · Song of Solomon 6
eras.name: Unique Among Women — Beautiful as Tirzah
eras.dates: The lovers reunite, and the beloved is celebrated as uniquely favored above every queen and concubine. (The Hebrew text's chapter division falls one verse earlier than most English translations, marked inline in the NET text itself as “(7:1)”.)

events.title: I Am My Lover's, and My Lover Is Mine — Unique Among Women
events.detail: The maidens ask where the lover has gone, and the Beloved answers with the mutual-belonging refrain again, before the lover praises her as unique and unrivaled even among sixty queens and eighty concubines.

verses.text: “But she is unique, my dove, my perfect one! She is the special daughter of her mother; she is the favorite of the one who bore her.”

eras.label: Era Seven · Song of Solomon 7
eras.name: How Beautiful Are Your Sandaled Feet — I Am My Beloved's, and He Desires Me
eras.dates: A final extended physical description moves from feet to head, closing in an unambiguous declaration of desire. (Numbered starting at 6:13 and 7:1 in most English translations, marked inline in the NET text as “(7:1)” and “(7:2)”.)

events.title: I Am My Beloved's, and He Desires Me
events.detail: The lover praises his beloved from her sandaled feet upward in the most physically explicit description in the book, and she responds by inviting him to the countryside and vineyards, declaring plainly that she belongs to him and he desires her.

verses.text: “I am my beloved's, and he desires me!”

eras.label: Era Eight · Song of Solomon 8
eras.name: Love Is as Strong as Death — Set Me as a Seal Upon Your Heart
eras.dates: The book closes with its most theologically resonant statement on love's power, followed by a closing dialogue about a sister's protection and a final call to the lover

events.title: Love Is as Strong as Death — Many Waters Cannot Quench Love
events.detail: The book's most quoted passage declares love as strong as death and as unrelenting as the grave, a blazing flame that floodwaters cannot quench and that no wealth could ever purchase — the closest the book comes to direct reflection on love's ultimate nature.

verses.text: “Love is as strong as death… Surging waters cannot quench love; floodwaters cannot overflow it.”

events.title: I Was a Wall — Make Haste, My Beloved
events.detail: The Beloved's brothers recall protecting their younger sister's honor, she affirms she was indeed a 'wall' who found favor in her lover's eyes, and the book closes with her final, unresolved call for him to come away with her like a gazelle on the mountains.

verses.text: “Make haste, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices.”
